tests.test: P01 noticing distance: run > walk > crouch (resting hound, corridor)
P02 light beam makes a walker easier to notice (hound)
P03 standing still: a hound that is not looking never finds a silent standing player 300px away behind it
P04 walls block sight: a hound never SEES a player through a wall at 150px
P05 hearing: a running player is heard through a wall (hound turns to it); a crouch-walker at the same spot is not
P06 hearing radius: sliding / vaulting / landing are loud events, a standing player is silent
P07 exhausted breathing is audible only close by
P08 memory: the last known position is used, then goes stale; the hound gives up and goes back to roaming
P09 no impossible information: a silent player two rooms away leaves no trace in a roaming hound's memory
P10 social awareness: a second player behind walls, silent, is not counted as a threat; a runner approaching is
P11 personality: same species, different individuals (trait variation within bounds)
P12 traversal caps: hound vaults, smiler vaults slower, nobody squeezes through wall holes without CAN_USE_TIGHT_GAPS; crawl only when allowed
H01 bait a lunge and sidestep: a late sidestep beats it most of the time; standing still does not
H02 no i-frames: a lunge that connects catches you whatever you were doing (walking/running); a slide can pass under it
H03 chase outcomes in the long corridor: a fresh runner with a head start lasts; an exhausted one is caught fast
H04 lunges start only when in range, roughly aligned and with a clear line
H05 poor sharp turning: the hound turns much slower at full speed than at a crawl
H06 after a missed lunge it recovers (skids, turns slowly) before it runs again
H07 hound state coverage: every state of the framework is reached by emergent play (no scripting of state changes)
H08 searching is logical: it starts at the last known position, fans out around it, and does not home in on a quiet crouching player
H09 the wall impact only ever happens against a wall that is really there
H10 exhausted prey: variant D only ever for a player with nothing left (and is the usual end for one caught from behind)
H11 no repeated identical death selection (variant history is respected)
H12 after a kill: it is worked up (EXCITED), then feeds; an intruder at the body is guarded against and hunted
H13 pack instinct: hounds near each other share a pack id, and one hound sounding off draws the others
H14 far hounds sleep and wake: no perception when far; awake when a player is near
SM01 light: a light carrier it can see is chased after a wind-up; the same person without a light is watched, not chased
SM02 strikes only on canon triggers: a quiet still person is never struck; a fast retreat in front of it (panic) or a loud noise close by is
SM03 eye contact: watched, it holds; backing away slowly while watching it gets you let go (it withdraws, no strike)
SM04 no hidden position: an unsensed player moved elsewhere changes nothing the Smiler does (tick by tick)
SM05 lost player: it goes where it last had them (with an uncertainty), not where they really went
SM06 light lead: drawn to what it observed (an uncertain region), and the same observations replayed with the carrier far away give identical decisions
SM07 wall occlusion: a torch lighting the far side of a wall draws nothing; the smiler stays where it is
SM08 infrared OFF vs HIGH: identical Smiler decisions (camcorders raised, infrared written everywhere a client could put it)
SM09 attention: a one-frame glance does nothing; through a wall nothing; sustained eye contact (with line of sight) holds it
SM10 hold is counterplay, not immunity: standing and staring, it creeps in and drifts sideways; a fixed gaze loses it; up close a small sound triggers it
SM11 multiplayer: one watches it in the dark, another walks about with a light - it works on the light, settles (no flicker), and a lit player it has never seen never wins
SM12 personality: bounded, deterministic per seed, and no extreme tiers
SM13 state validity over long mixed runs: finite, valid targets and states, legal transitions, never inside walls, never stuck
SM14 no teleporting: every move is walked (bounded per tick), whatever it is doing
SM15 presentation: no limbs; the face glow is its own channel (not the generic entity alpha); no aggression UI outside debug
tests.note: repaired debug-gate fixture; runtime code unchanged

tests.test: SM16 multiplayer: a light elsewhere draws it off somebody it only watches in the dark (once - no back-and-forth); eye contact keeps it
SM17 close-range pressure: holding its eyes does not let you walk up to it - walking, crouching or inching in on it ends in a strike; standing still or backing away does not
C01 quick or play depends on the situation: others approaching -> almost always a quick kill; an isolated victim -> the hound may toy with it (the canon Smiler never plays)
C02 CAUGHT is not DEAD: a played-with victim stays alive and held; the next major decision comes after a tense 4-21 s and never in a rush
C03 false hope: a released victim that runs may be hunted again (hounds; the canon Smiler never plays, so never releases)
C04 interruption: someone running up with a light changes its mind within a moment - it kills (a canon Smiler is drawn to the light, not scared off)
C05 after a quick kill it reads the room: with others coming it defends, attacks the next or leaves; alone it settles (the Smiler lingers, then returns to the dark)
C06 the death itself: one kill per life, the record carries variant / geometry, the body is where the victim fell, no repeat kills
C07 spawn protection and admin god mode: nothing captures a protected player; unprotected, the very same attack lands
C08 two hunters, one victim: exactly one capture; the other reacts to the kill (it does not double-kill)
Y01 level of detail: perception runs at full rate near a player, at a reduced rate further out, and not at all while an entity is far away
Y02 performance: the shipped population and a stress population fit the frame budget
Y03 snapshot size: what goes over the wire every 50 ms stays small (entities are quantised; nothing per-player-private is sent)
Y04 stuck entities: one embedded in a wall is set back on open floor and one that cannot go anywhere does not stand frozen forever
Y05 turning and snapping: headings change smoothly (no per-tick flips), speeds change within acceleration limits
Y06 no wall clipping: over long emergent runs no entity ever stands inside solid geometry (vaults excepted)
Y07 pop-in: a smiler only appears or vanishes by fading (its visibility changes at a bounded rate); entities are only ever spawned out of sight
Y08 determinism: the same seed and the same inputs give the same world (no stray randomness, safe for tests and replays)
Y09 population caps and bodies over a long session: at most 3 hounds and 5 smilers; one body per player, at most 24
Y10 bodies persist for the configured time: forever by default, or BODY_TTL seconds
A01 preview death: every variant of both killers is played exactly as asked, through the real kill path (record, events, entity left in a sane state)
A02 preview works through god mode, spawn protection and a frozen world; refuses honestly (no wall near, already dead, already caught, everything busy)
A03 preview uses the nearest free entity (population unchanged) and only spawns one when none exists (and removes it again if the preview is refused)
A04 capture style override: AUTO leaves the decision to the entity, QUICK makes every catch a kill, PLAY makes every catch a held victim (then the normal decision)
A05 the AI event log: state changes, catches, kills and lamp failures are written down with a running number; readers get only what is new; the log stays short
K01 a hound that kills stays on its kill for the whole death (does not move, does not take the witness standing right there)
K02 ...and then it decides: an aggressive hound goes for the witness after the kill, not during it
K03 every variant commits for its own length (A 4.5 / B 4.7 / C 4.3 / D 4.5 s)
K04 the victim's report of where the animation left the hound is used only if it is close and clear
NV01 A/B/E reachable targets are reached: 40 hound routes (292 px/s) and 20 smiler routes across rooms, corners and doorways
NV02 solids are never entered and nothing is NaN (all routes, doorways and chases): no tick inside the collision margin, no emergency un-embedding
NV03 C/D/J doorway traversal: every narrow doorway, approached head-on and at 30/60 degrees, both species: all through, no ramming, little touching
NV04 paths simplify when safe: routes are string-pulled (far fewer waypoints than grid cells) and never cut through a wall
NV05 F/G/H single-obstacle loops: laps round a pillar / bar / cross / L-shaped wall do not beat a hunting hound (real AI, real stamina)
NV06 I rapid reversals through a doorway: a player hopping back and forth through a door every 1.2 s does not cause a repath storm and is caught
NV07 K/L traversal capabilities: routes only use cells the species may use (smilers never crawl), vault links are costed, not free
NV08 M two bodies through one doorway: they pass, press a little, never sit inside each other
NV09 N a runner through 3+ rooms (real AI): caught every time, no ramming, little touching, no repath storm
NV10 O line of sight lost round a corner (real AI): the hound heads for where it last knew the runner was going, not where the runner really is, and does not freeze
NV11 stuck recovery: a hound wedged nose-first into a concave corner / against a pillar gets out and arrives (no teleport)
NV12 cost: navigation per tick stays cheap and path searches stay rare in a busy world (3 hounds, 5 smilers, 4 players moving, 120 s)
C1 losing sight does not erase memory: 3 s after the prey vanishes the hound still has it (confidence, position, heading) and is still after it
C2 it reaches the last known position (or where the prey was heading from it) after losing sight
C3 it does not track the hidden prey exactly: after losing it, its goals come from memory and sound, never from where the prey really is
C4 noise gives the prey away: a prey that has slipped away quietly and then breaks into a run is re-acquired by ear at once (no new detection wait)
C5 silent hiding can succeed, and good decisions beat bad ones: out of sight, going quiet and moving on gets away far more often than hiding right where it lost you
C6 crouching is not invisibility: a crouched, still player in the dark right in front of an unaware hound is noticed
C7 repeated corner cheese fails: ducking back and forth round one corner is not a way to be safe
C8 counter / shelf / machine loops fail: laps round a vaultable obstacle do not keep a hunting hound off (it vaults or cuts across)
C9 / C10 an exhausted runner is far more vulnerable; a fresh one can still make distance
C11 / C12 crawlspaces: a crawling player gets in and out through every wall hole and under every table, continuously (no teleport), never inside a wall
C13 an entity never enters a crawlspace it cannot use: smilers never go under furniture, nothing goes through a wall hole
C14 / C17 an entity that cannot follow into a crawlspace remembers the prey went in and goes round to the other side
C15 an entity that can crawl goes through a crawlspace: a hound goes under a table
C16 a body inside a crawlspace is not visible from across the room, only close by
C18 memory eventually decays: when the prey gets away, the hound gives up for a stated reason and its confidence has run out
C19 / C20 no geometry clipping and no NaN in chases, searches and crawlspace escapes
B1 (test infrastructure) the escape bench calls a test hook exactly once per simulation step
L1 lifecycle: a living, free player cannot respawn
L2 lifecycle: a dead player respawns (at the spawn point, full stamina, protected)
L3 lifecycle: held in a capture but not dead - no respawn and no new run (the capture ends in a death or a release)
L4 lifecycle: an admin revive leaves one respawn (and only one)
L5 movement check: open floor and short hops pass; through a wall does not; a long hop needs a real route that short
L6 the death plan numbers are one table: the bundle's death class and the server fallback read the same knock / drag / blows as v22 did
L7 the server fallback corpse is the physical death run to rest: deterministic, on open floor, gear and hands present
L8 lifecycle (v22.2): held - leave is refused too, so leave -> join cannot escape; walking out (disconnect) forfeits the capture as a death
L9 lifecycle (v22.2): a living player starts a new run only through the NEW RUN sequence (vanish, 2 s or more, then leave / join), once per 30 s
E1 walls stop light: a torch lights nothing and gives no evidence on the far side of a wall
E2 a lit wall seen without the person: an anonymous lead (no player, wide uncertainty), not a target and not a record
E3 the light source in view gives an anonymous source lead; only sight of the person then names it
E4 light off: no new light evidence, but what it already has stays (and fades like any memory)
E5 hidden-position invariance: an unsensed player moved elsewhere changes nothing the hound does
E6 observation replay: the carrier somewhere else, the same observations replayed -> the same leads and decisions (no back-projection)
E7 the camcorder emits no visible light: no beam, no light evidence, no glare bonus - its raised state is presentation only
E8 eye contact: seen and facing it -> detected; facing away, or a wall between -> not
E9 target commitment: it does not switch to somebody else inside the dwell unless it has truly lost its prey
E10 bounded and valid: leads <= 6, evidence <= 4 per record, all numbers finite, confidences in [0,1], over long mixed runs
I1 infrared never reaches the simulation: ai.js / sim.js do not name it; server.js stores it on the connection, not on the player
I2 toggling infrared alone changes no AI decision (OFF vs HIGH, same world, same players, tick by tick)
I3 a raised camcorder is no light to the AI: no lit player, no light evidence from it
2E H1 identified human with flashlight warrants pursuit
2E H2 swept beam reaches Hound from behind: attention then identification
2E H3 hidden carrier: anonymous light investigation; replay cannot back-project
2E H4 solid wall blocks direct beam and impossible evidence
2E H5 IR OFF vs HIGH: identical complete decisions each tick
2E H6 hidden corner branches cannot change prediction
2E H7 fresh running after loss causes hearing-based reacquisition
2E H8 silent hidden reposition does not cause magical following
2E H9 nearby noisy hiding is exposed through real movement footsteps
2E H10 failed search reduces confidence and ends within finite budget
2E H11 stable multiplayer target, then meaningful switch after loss and dwell
2E H12 listening is watchdog-safe; blocked movement still recovers
2E H13 long-run finite states, valid targets, bounded memory and collision
2E H14 gaze intimidation is temporary, breaks on looking away and cannot be toggled to refill
2E H15 flashlight off stops new light observations without deleting an identified human
2E H16 bounded deterministic traits; private HP and inventory cannot change decisions
2E H17 social sound carries no prey identity or shared memory
